from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Refresher: The Transformation Paradigm", [
            "Square matrices reorient coordinates in the same dimension.",
            "This transformation acts as a map for vectors.",
            "Think of rotating a vector like a compass."
        ])
        
        # Define axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], x_length=4, y_length=4)
        grid_lines = VGroup(*[Line(axes.c2p(-2, i), axes.c2p(2, i), stroke_opacity=0.3) for i in range(-2, 3)],
                            *[Line(axes.c2p(i, -2), axes.c2p(i, 2), stroke_opacity=0.3) for i in range(-2, 3)])
        self.place_in_area(grid_lines, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        compass = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(compass, 'A6', scale_factor=0.3)
        
        i_hat = Vector(axes.c2p(1, 0) - axes.c2p(0, 0), color="#FF4444")
        j_hat = Vector(axes.c2p(0, 1) - axes.c2p(0, 0), color="#44FF44")
        basis = VGroup(i_hat, j_hat)
        self.place_in_area(basis, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_lines), FadeIn(basis), FadeIn(compass))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        target_i = Vector(axes.c2p(0.707, 0.707) - axes.c2p(0, 0), color="#FF4444")
        target_j = Vector(axes.c2p(-0.707, 0.707) - axes.c2p(0, 0), color="#44FF44")
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(i_hat, target_i),
            ReplacementTransform(j_hat, target_j),
            grid_lines.animate.apply_matrix([[0.707, -0.707], [0.707, 0.707]])
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        new_compass = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg")
        new_compass.rotate(PI/4)
        self.place_at_grid(new_compass, 'A6', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(compass, new_compass))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Tall matrices map low dimensions into high dimensions.",
            "This embedding injects a vector into a larger space.",
            "A 2D shape becomes a 3D thin billboard."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mapping Up: Embedding into Higher Dimensions", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors for lecture lines
        colors = ["#FFADAD", "#CAFFBF", "#FDFFB6"]
        
        # Setup 3D Scene elements
        axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], z_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        grid_2d = VGroup(*[Line(start=[-1, i, 0], end=[1, i, 0]) for i in np.arange(-1, 1.1, 0.5)] +
                         [Line(start=[i, -1, 0], end=[i, 1, 0]) for i in np.arange(-1, 1.1, 0.5)])
        grid_2d.set_color(BLUE)
        
        matrix_tex = MathTex(r"\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \\ e & f \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} X \\ Y \\ Z \end{pmatrix}")
        matrix_tex.set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'D3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(grid_2d, 'D3', scale_factor=0.4)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(grid_2d))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1]))
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_tex, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(matrix_tex))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2]))
        
        # Transformation: Lift grid into 3D space
        grid_3d = grid_2d.copy().set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(Transform(grid_2d, grid_3d))
        
        # Confirm rotation
        self.set_camera_orientation(phi=75 * DEGREES, theta=45 * DEGREES)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Wide matrices map high dimensions down to low.",
            "This projection compresses data, sacrificing depth.",
            "Like a 3D object captured on 2D film."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mapping Down: The Concept of Projection", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create objects
        cube = Cube(fill_opacity=0.5, color="#44CCFF").scale(0.6)
        matrix = MathTex(r"A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}", color=WHITE)
        plane = Square(side_length=2, fill_opacity=0.3, color="#FFCC44").rotate(PI/2, axis=RIGHT)
        
        # Initial positions
        self.place_at_grid(cube, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, "E2")
        self.place_at_grid(plane, "B5")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#44CCFF"))
        self.play(Create(cube), Write(matrix))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFCC44"))
        self.play(FadeIn(plane))
        # Project cube onto plane
        projection = cube.copy().set_color("#FFCC44").set_opacity(0.8)
        self.play(
            cube.animate.scale(0.1).move_to(self.grid["B5"]),
            Transform(projection, Rectangle(height=1.2, width=1.2, color="#FFCC44", fill_opacity=0.5).move_to(self.grid["B5"]))
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the 'Transformation Flow'", [
            "Matrices bridge these differing dimensional realms.",
            "They control expansion into higher spaces.",
            "They also govern compression back into lower ones."
        ])
        
        # 2D Grid
        grid_2d = VGroup(*[
            Line(np.array([-1, i, 0]), np.array([1, i, 0])) for i in range(-1, 2)
        ], *[
            Line(np.array([i, -1, 0]), np.array([i, 1, 0])) for i in range(-1, 2)
        ]).set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(grid_2d, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)

        # 3D object placeholder
        cube = Cube(side_length=1.5).set_color(RED)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        bridge = Text("Matrix Bridge", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(bridge, 'E4')
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_2d), Write(bridge))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(grid_2d),
            FadeIn(cube),
            Transform(bridge, Text("Expansion: 2D -> 3D", font_size=20, color=GREEN))
        )
        self.place_at_grid(bridge, 'E4')
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(cube),
            FadeIn(grid_2d),
            Transform(bridge, Text("Compression: 3D -> 2D", font_size=20, color=ORANGE))
        )
        self.place_at_grid(bridge, 'E4')
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: Why Non-Square Matters", [
            "Non-square matrices are powerful mathematical engines.",
            "They enable viewpoints, compression, and feature extraction.",
            "Crucial for understanding modern machine learning."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # High-dimensional cloud of dots (represented as 2D dots for complexity)
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color=BLUE) for _ in range(50)])
        for d in dots:
            d.move_to(np.array([np.random.uniform(-1, 1), np.random.uniform(-1, 1), 0]) * 1.5)
        self.place_in_area(dots, "A1", "C6", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(dots))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transformation effect (simplistic projection)
        target_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color=GREEN) for _ in range(50)])
        for d in target_dots:
            d.move_to(np.array([np.random.uniform(-1, 1), 0, 0]) * 1.5)
        self.place_in_area(target_dots, "D1", "E6", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Transform(dots, target_dots))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Classification labels
        label = Text("Classification", color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "F3", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Geometric Interpretation of Non-Square Matrices as Dimensional Transformations
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in linear algebra or computer graphics

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresher: The Transformation Paradigm
sections.content: Define a square matrix as a coordinate system reorientation within the same dimension (e.g., rotation/scaling in 2D). Introduce the concept of a 'Linear Map' where inputs are mapped to outputs.
sections.example: A 2x2 matrix acting on a 2D arrow, rotating it like a compass needle.

sections.title: Mapping Up: Embedding into Higher Dimensions
sections.content: Explain the concept of 'Embedding'. A tall matrix (rows > columns) takes a low-dimensional vector and maps it into a higher-dimensional space, effectively acting as an injection.
sections.example: A 3x2 matrix taking a flat 2D 'stick figure' and placing it into a 3D room, essentially turning the 2D image into a thin billboard in 3D space.

sections.title: Mapping Down: The Concept of Projection
sections.content: Explain the concept of 'Projection'. A wide matrix (columns > rows) takes a high-dimensional vector and maps it into a lower-dimensional space, causing information 'compression' or 'flattening'.
sections.example: A 2x3 matrix acting as a camera: a 3D cat is mapped onto a 2D photographic sensor, where depth is lost in the projection.

sections.title: Visualizing the 'Transformation Flow'
sections.content: Synthesize the two concepts using a visual animation flow. Show the transition from 2D -> 3D (Expansion) and 3D -> 2D (Compression). Emphasize that the matrix is the 'bridge' between these differing realms.
sections.example: A 3D mechanical robot arm folding its reach into a 2D plane controlled by a matrix transformation.

sections.title: Conclusion: Why Non-Square Matters
sections.content: Summarize that non-square matrices are the mathematical engines for changing viewpoints, data compression, and feature extraction in machine learning.
sections.example: A neural network layer represented as a matrix mapping thousands of pixels (high dim) down to a simple classification score (low dim).
